subject: AtlasOne renewal — usage mosaic & latency-anchored offer
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@atlasone.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasOne renewal — usage mosaic & latency-anchored offer

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I pulled together a short recap of usage signals and a proposal to simplify your renewal while addressing the latency-sensitive routes you flagged. Attachments: atlasone_q1_usage.csv (token breakdown by endpoint), latency_bench.pdf (our internal p95 checks across model mix).

Quick highlights from Q1 usage (attached):
- Total tokens: ~560M (70% generation, 30% embeddings/rerank).
- Peak concurrency: 220 rps across inference routes; p95 latency reported ~270ms on the prompt-heavy pipeline.
- KV cache hit ~12% for your conversational flow; prefetching should raise that substantially.

Two recommended threads for the renewal/upsell:
1) Commit + headroom: a 12-month committed token band (700M) with a defined burst lane (extra 150M) that keeps unit price stable and funds predictable capacity.
2) Latency SLA & pilot: a 6-week dedicated pilot for your latency-critical routes on our Dedicated tier (p95 target 180ms). If p95 > 200ms in production, a small SLA credit mechanism kicks in (we can define exact %).

Can you confirm: (a) procurement timeline, (b) whether the pilot needs to be in us-west-2 specifically, and (c) any VP/SEC contacts for SOC2 evidence if your procurement team will request it?

If that sounds reasonable, I can circulate a succinct amendment and an invoice estimate for the pilot.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com]

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick summary and the attachments. Quick answers up front: procurement will start internal approvals next week; region ideally us-west-2 but we can evaluate us-east-1 if capacity constraints show up. Our ops lead Rajiv is cc'd — he will dig into the latency bench and confirm cache feasibility.

A few clarifying questions from our side:
- For the Dedicated pilot, what does the onboarding look like? How long to move traffic and rollback if we see regressions?
- Can the pilot be scoped to only the conversation route (the one with prefill + multi-turn history) so we don't need full account migration?
- If we agree to a 12-month commit, can we structure quarterly true-ups rather than an annual true-up?

We'll pull procurement into the thread once Rajiv and I align on the pilot scope.

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Product, AtlasOne
emily@atlasone.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@atlasone.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasOne renewal — usage mosaic & latency-anchored offer

Emily / Jordan —

Thanks — Ben from Solutions here. A few technical notes and an operational suggestion to make the pilot low-risk:

Technical bullets:
- Onboarding: we can route only the conversation endpoint to a dedicated pool within 48 hours (feature-flagged). Rollback is immediate via routing policy (DNS-level rollback + traffic split in the console) — typical failover under 5 minutes.
- KV cache: enabling prefix caching should lift your cache-hit from 12% to ~45% for multi-turn flows based on similar customers. That would lower token compute by ~18% on those routes.
- Model mix: recommend we pin the pilot to the smaller-parameter variant we validated in the bench (gpt-small-v2-quant). If quality checks against your eval set pass, we move to standard variant for broader traffic.

Operational proposal (pilot + commit):
- Pilot: 6 weeks, dedicated pool, scope limited to /v1/conversation route. Estimated pilot cost: $9,500 (compute + reserved pilot margin).
- Renewal commit: 12-month band = 700M tokens at discounted unit rate (15% discount vs pay-as-you-go). Quarterly true-ups allowed (we'll reconcile each quarter, adjust next quarter's billing).
- Burst lane: 150M tokens available on-demand at 40% surcharge to committed unit price.

If that aligns, Jordan/Kim can draft a 1-page amendment and a short SOW for the pilot.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Emily Park <emily@atlasone.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@atlasone.com>, procurement@atlasone.com
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasOne renewal — usage mosaic & latency-anchored offer

Thanks Ben — that model mix and the rollback details make me comfortable. Procurement (procurement@atlasone.com) is cc'd — per their ask, please include in the amendment:
- Specific SLA language for p95 latency on the dedicated route (we'd like the 180ms target and a sliding credit scale if p95 > 200ms).
- Quarterly reconciliation clause and the ability to move unused committed tokens into the next quarter (not annual).
- Security addendum: SOC2 report + standard pen test summary (high level).

I've attached procurement_requirements.docx with our redlines on commercial terms we typically require. We'll need an invoice estimate for the pilot so procurement can start approvals.

Can you send a short amendment + pilot SOW and an invoice estimate by EOD Monday? That would keep approvals on track for mid-April roll.

—Emily

Emily / team —

Great—appreciate the clarity. Summary / next steps below:

Summary of proposal:
- Pilot: 6-week dedicated pilot scoped to /v1/conversation route. Pilot cost estimate: $9,500 (invoice line item will include compute + reserved pilot fee).
- Renewal: 12-month committed band = 700M tokens with quarterly true-ups. Unused tokens roll forward to the next quarter. Burst lane: 150M tokens at 40% surcharge.
- SLA: Target p95 180ms for the dedicated route; proposed credit scale (example): p95 between 180–200ms = 5% credit; p95 > 200ms = 12% credit (we will formalize language in the amendment).
- Security: we'll provide SOC2 Type II report and a summary of recent penetration test results as part of the Security Addendum.

Requested items from AtlasOne to start paperwork:
1) Procurement contact (full name + billing address + PO process) — procurement@atlasone.com is copied; please confirm a PO contact.
2) Approval to schedule pilot start window: proposed 19 Apr 2027 — 31 May 2027.
3) Any required contract template clauses from legal (if you have a preferred amendment template).

I will circulate a 1-page amendment, the pilot SOW, and an invoice estimate by EOD Monday (2027-03-15). I'll include the DocuSign link and the HubSpot deal id in that email.
